checks: The proven ray-supported perturbation changes membership in finitely many O(t) strips. On compact patches in the relative interior of a genuine facet, the other rows stay slack, giving signed speed δ_j(r)/‖r‖. Missing facets meet the old body in lower-dimensional sets and contribute o(t), as do old edges and strip intersections. In d=1 the endpoints have counting measure.

At fixed endpoints all speeds are nonnegative, so the normal segment lies on the outward side and the limiting indicator is the correct one at a coincident fixed cap. For a pure-base cap its restriction is constant, including the closed equality case.

For signed velocities and a facet-null cap plane, the original strict cap margin almost everywhere determines its indicator on the whole small strip. A threshold change of fixed speed preserves that pointwise limit, proving the displayed difference between the two measures at the same moving cap.

Planar exposed lengths interpolate linearly by the Minkowski sum of parallel segments or points. The Green sums follow by the discrete second differences of the stated quadratic and cubic with Dirichlet boundary. Rational replay independently verifies the mass formula for N=2 through 23.

The triangle/square endpoint coefficients are (1,1), (0,1), and (1,0) on the three stated ray groups. The two mode columns give (1,1), (4/9,5/9), and (5/9,4/9). Summing the four positive-cardinal modes gives two.
